correctness.rationale: The exact two-adjacent-pair-deletion definition is fixed with nonoverlapping blocks. A transversal H meets every received ball, forcing an upper bound by its size. For n=7,9, the odd-position pigeonhole and a distinct-neighbor matching yield transversals of sizes 4,8. For n=8, a repeated aligned pair or one of six complement/reversal symmetry cases yields a transversal of size 4. Period-two words attain the n=6,7,8 bounds; a two-word constant code attains n=5. The eight-word n=9 linear code is generated by three independent nine-bit rows, and its eight checked 32-bit output masks are pairwise disjoint and together equal 0xffffffff. The independently implemented Python and C++ packaged verifiers enumerate every input at n=5..9, checks all orbit witnesses and verifies the perfect received-word partition. No extrapolation to n>9 is made.

originality.rationale: This is a new exact short-block maximum-size profile for a channel already defined in the literature, with a perfect linear eight-word length-nine construction and an exact two-length plateau. The same-channel 2026 paper provides known n=6 and wider structural bounds but no claim covering the length-seven-to-nine optimum/perfectness pair. Earlier 2024 and 2025 full primary PDFs address asymptotic constructions and sequence reconstruction respectively. Semantic published-record and exact web searches identified no same or stronger result. No search establishes absolute novelty: residual risk is explicitly retained.

Database search coverage and public indexing cannot establish originality in an absolute sense.

value.rationale: The exact initial range is naturally determined by the first five admissible blocklengths of an important synchronization-error model. The maximum remains four across lengths six through eight and first increases to eight at length nine. Beyond the numerical optimum, the nine-bit linear code partitions all 32 possible received words into four singleton and four size-seven deletion balls; this is a perfect unequal-ball covering/packing benchmark. Both the plateau and perfect-code transition are meaningful short-block structural facts not implied by asymptotic rates, rather than arbitrary parameter slices.
